meta.title: Safari Zone
meta.description: The hub's Safari Zone: the 60-slot Pokémon pool (slots 0–44 regular, 45–59 legendary), the four ways Pokémon enter it, the temporary illegal ribbon that gates every push, the priority and eviction system that decides who stays, and the Legends Cave flow for re-battling the legendaries you've caught. All of the mechanics are identical between Vanilla and EX — what differs is which legendary species exist to catch.

prose.heading: The Safari Zone in the hub
prose.text: The Safari Area is one of the four hub areas that already exists when you start, always attached to the Town Exit (which is itself attached to the Labs) — so the zone is always two hops from the Labs and never directly next to them. Its introduction tutorial plays the first time you visit. The zone is a catch practice ground for the Pokémon of your own save: up to 6 of the pooled Pokémon are visible in the grass at a time, battles are safari-style catch battles (you pick which ball to throw from your bag mid-battle), and a sign in the area lets you view the current regular pool in a special Pokédex view or “Dismiss” all regular Pokémon at once.

prose.heading: The 60-slot pool
prose.text: Beyond the 60 slots, 16 additional “custom” slots let unique/gift Pokémon keep their special sets while they sit in the pool. A temporary “illegal ribbon” (the code reuses the Marine ribbon slot) is what gates every push into the pool: a mon is only added if it does not carry the ribbon, and every successful push stamps it — so the same mon can't be added twice. The ribbon is also stamped on every member of your pre-run party and every Day Care mon at the start of every run — that is what keeps your home team out of the pool (see The run-start illegal ribbon). (An outdated comment in the constants says “45–49 are for legends”, but every allocation and reset loop in the code uses the full 45–59 range.)

prose.heading: How Pokémon enter the pool
prose.text: Four events push Pokémon into the pool — two while a run is active, one when the run ends, and a low-priority discard path. Every push goes through the same gate — the run-start illegal ribbon — detailed after the four cards.

prose.heading: Priority and eviction
prose.text: A mon that has only been caught and immediately released scores 0 — and a discarded mon enters at that same 0, so discards are the first out unless they are shiny, in which case the +30 bonus makes them as safe as any long-kept mon.

prose.heading: The Legends Cave
prose.text: Completing the “True Legend” quest (catch a legendary during an adventure) grants the hidden “Legend Cave” upgrade, which puts a cave entrance on the Safari Area. From there, 10 of a liked-flavor Pokéblock can be turned into a wild, catchable battle with a pooled legendary.

records.name: Released from your party
records.short: Mid-run — releasing a mon pushes it straight in.
records.description: While a run is active, releasing a Pokémon from your party immediately pushes it into the pool (except during the endless trainer mode after the top of the boss ladder) — if the mon isn't wearing its run-start illegal ribbon. A released pre-run party mon goes to the lab instead and comes back with the rest of your pre-run party when the run ends. Legendaries go to the legendary slots, everything else to the regular slots.

records.name: Fainted and removed mid-run
records.short: Mid-run — 0-HP party mons are pushed out after a win.
records.description: After every battle you win in a run, any party Pokémon left at 0 HP is removed from your party and pushed into the pool the same way a release would be — again gated by the run-start illegal ribbon: a fainted pre-run party mon goes to the lab instead and is restored when the run ends.

records.name: When the run ends
records.short: Run end — the run-acquired party, then the Day Care, is added.
records.description: When an adventure ends (victory or defeat), every Pokémon in your party that isn't wearing its run-start illegal ribbon is added to the pool — in practice, the mons you picked up during the run — and then the same for your Day Care. Your pre-run party and Day Care wear the ribbon, so they are skipped and instead restored from the pre-run snapshot the run took of your hub state — a run you lose still returns your team, and the mons you caught restock the Safari Zone. Edge case: the Starter Bag upgrade hands you your random starter after the snapshot but before the ribbon stamping, so a starter that survives the whole run is neither added to the pool (it carries the ribbon) nor restored to your party (it isn't in the snapshot) — it is lost entirely.

records.name: Discarded after capture
records.short: Per catch — a discarded catch enters at priority 0.
records.description: If you catch a wild Pokémon and choose to discard it instead of keeping it, it is pushed into the pool at low priority (0) — it is evicted before any normally-added mon unless it is shiny, where it earns the +30 shiny bonus. (During a catching contest, non-shiny discards are skipped entirely.)

records.name: The run-start illegal ribbon
records.short: A temp ribbon gates every push — pre-run mons are stamped at run start, so only run-acquired mons can enter.
records.description: Every push into the pool first checks the mon's temporary illegal ribbon (the code reuses the Marine ribbon slot): a mon carrying it is skipped, and every successful push stamps it, so a given mon can enter the pool at most once. At the start of every run — after the run has snapshotted your pre-run hub state (party, Day Care, bag and money) and, with the Starter Bag upgrade, handed out your random starter — the ribbon is stamped on every member of the current party and on every Day Care mon. That snapshot is what your hub state is restored to when the run ends, so pre-run mons can never enter the pool: they simply come back, and a pre-run mon released or fainted mid-run goes to the lab instead of the pool. Two other paths stamp the ribbon mid-run: picking up a mon from the lab (it already sits in the pool from its faint, so the stamp prevents a duplicate entry) and snagging a trainer mon under the Snag Curse. The edge case this creates: your Starter Bag starter is handed out after the snapshot but before the stamping, so a starter that survives the whole run is neither added to the pool (it carries the ribbon) nor restored to your party (it isn't in the snapshot) — the Pokémon is lost entirely. A snagged trainer mon that survives to run end meets the same fate.

records.name: Slot layout (60 pool slots)
records.description: The pool is exactly 60 slots: 0–44 are regular slots (45 total — the only slots the open zone spawns from, cycling through them in order), and 45–59 are legendary slots (15 total — reachable only via the Legends Cave). A separate table of 16 “custom” slots maps unique/gift Pokémon so they keep their special sets while pooled. (The in-code comment “45-49 are for legends” is outdated; the allocation, reset and any-legends loops all use 45–59.)
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L806-810 / @origin/expansion L808-812 (ROGUE_SAFARI_TOTAL_MONS 60, LEGENDS_START_INDEX 45, TOTAL_CUSTOM_MONS 16); src/rogue_safari.c @vanilla L313-375 / @origin/expansion L313-375 (AllocSafariMonSlotFor: regular → 0..44, legendary → 45..59)

records.name: Priority and eviction
records.description: Each entry's priority is (levels gained since capture × 2) ÷ 5 — a freshly caught-and-released mon scores 0; shinies add a flat +30 (half the pool size); and any IV bonus from IV-boosting charms is stripped before the mon is stored. When a range (regular or legendary) is full, all mons sharing the lowest priority are evicted together as a batch, the survivors' priorities are each decremented by the batch count, and one freed slot takes the new arrival. Regular and legendary ranges never evict each other.

score.note: the IV bonus from IV-boosting charms is stripped before the mon is stored

eviction: A range (regular or legendary) is full
Every mon sharing the lowest priority is evicted as a batch
Every survivor's priority drops by the batch count
One freed slot takes the new arrival
records.source: src/rogue_safari.c @vanilla L37-92 (PushBoxMonInternal: priority at L82, charm strip at L48, shiny +30 at L88) and L313-375 (eviction batching in AllocSafariMonSlotFor) / @origin/expansion L37-92, L313-375

records.name: Legends Cave legendary catch
steps: Complete the “True Legend” quest (catch a legendary during an adventure) — its reward is the hidden “Legend Cave” upgrade, which adds the cave entrance to the Safari Area.
Enter the cave and talk to the odd statue. If no legendaries are in the pool, “the cave is silent.”
Choose “Make Offering” from the statue menu.
Pick the legendary you want from the special Pokédex view of your pooled legendaries.
Choose a Pokéblock to offer. Its flavor type must match one of the legendary's two types, or it “won't like that type of Pokéblock.”
Confirm the cost of 10 of that Pokéblock and scatter them near the statue.
The cave shakes, the legendary-appears theme plays, the cry rings out — and a wild battle with that legendary begins (safari-style, catchable).
Alternatively, “Dismiss Pokémon” clears every legendary out of the cave at once.
records.description: The Legends Cave is how legendaries in the pool (slots 45–59) become re-encounterable: a statue that turns 10 of a liked-flavor Pokéblock into a wild battle with the legendary you pick. The whole flow is identical between versions — what differs is the roster of legendaries that can exist in the pool, since EX adds every Gen 4–9 legendary, their alternate forms, and the Z-A Floettes on top of Vanilla's Gen 1–3 set.

differences.vanilla: Mechanically identical cave; the catchable legendaries are limited to the Gen 1–3 legendary species (and forms) that exist in the Vanilla build.
differences.ex: Same cave and flow, but the legendary encounter roster adds all Gen 4–9 legendaries, alternate forms and the Z-A Floettes — so far more species can fill slots 45–59.

records.name: View and dismiss the pool
records.description: The sign in the Safari Area offers two actions: “View Pokémon” opens the regular pool (slots 0–44) in a special Pokédex view showing each mon's name, level and shininess, and “Dismiss Pokémon” clears all regular pool entries at once (the Legends Cave has its own separate “Dismiss” for the legendary slots).
